To: Finance Committee 
From: Allen Ward, Deputy Director of Budget and Purchasing 
Subject: Culvert Inventory Task Order with Stillwater Environmental Engineering 
Date: November 23, 2026 
Stillwater Environmental Engineering, Inc. holds the Master Service contract for stormwater compliance.  
SEE was awarded the contract at the June 3, 2024, Finance Committee meeting for a three (3) year term 
through June 30, 2027. 
Engineering requests consideration for Stillwater Environmental Engineering to Inventory and collect data 
from approximately 420 Lewiston culverts to help the department  prioritize scheduling repairs  or 
replacement as needed. 
The City Council allocated funding for this Task Order from the Storm Water FY25 LCIP. 
It is recommen ded that the Culvert Inventory Task Order with Stillwater Environmental Engineering, 
Inc. be authorized in an amount not to exceed $46,200. 
There is adequate funding for this Task Order in the source identified in the Deputy City Engineer’s memo.

TO: Allen Ward, Purchasing Agent 
FROM: Peralie Burbank, PE, Assistant City Engineer 
DATE: November 17, 2026 
SUBJECT: Stillwater Environmental Engineering Task Order for Culvert Inventory 
There are 409 culverts in public rights-of-way currently mapped in the City’s GIS for 
which the City is responsible. (There are also culverts that are private and culverts 
owned or managed by the Maine Department of Transportation.) Of these 409 known 
culverts, only 35 have been inspected, and we have no information about material or 
diameter for over a quarter of them. Information about culverts is generally collected 
only when there is paving or other roadwork in the vicinity, or when they fail. 
Inventorying and collecting data about the culverts will allow the City to proactively 
repair or replace them before sinkholes or failures occur. This will provide cost savings 
by allowing us to schedule repairs grouped in a competitive contract and by preventing 
emergency repair costs.  
Stillwater Environmental Engineering holds the Master Service Agreement (Bid No. 
2024-015) for stormwater compliance. They have provided services for the City on 
several projects and have recently completed culvert inventories for others. We asked 
for an estimate for 420 culverts in case additional culverts are found that need to be 
added to our mapping. 
Public Works recommends approval of this task order. The costs associated with this 
project will be charged to the following account: 
Account No. Name of Account Amount to be Charged Current Balance Available 
6645-645140 Storm Drain Inspection $46,200.00 $46,421.84 
Please present for Finance Committee approval.

Please refer to our previous RFQ submission for relevant experience and team member qualiﬁcations for the tasks

Project Scope  
Task 1 - Field Collection 
Task 1.1 - Preliminary Document Review  
SEE personnel will prepare for the culvert inventory ﬁeld work by evaluating the existing information provided by 
the City of Lewiston. This information will be incorporated into a customized mobile app in order to facilitate the 
collection of geolocated data as detailed in Task 1.2.   SEE will meet with Lewiston GIS staff to con ﬁrm that the 
application created can be easily imported into the City’s existing GIS. 
For the completion of this task, SEE assumes that the City of Lewiston will provide the relevant existing culvert 
documentation. 
Task 1.2 - Field Collection 
After preliminary review, the locations of the known culverts will be imported into a customized mobile app for 
ﬁeld data collection. 
Following the creation and testing of the inspection form application, SEE Staff will inspect the road-crossing 
culverts identi ﬁed by the City of Lewiston. Our staff, including environmental interns, will use the mobile data 
collection tool Fulcrum for these inspections. This collection tool allows for data transfer between the ﬁeld 
application and ESRI GIS tools.  
Since the goal of this initial phase of work is to create an initial culvert database layer and not a comprehensive 
culvert assessment, the following data will be collected for each culvert:  
● Location and crossing identiﬁer; 
● Inlet and outlet size, type, and diameter; 
● Approximate crossing length;
● General crossing condition observations (Good, Fair, Poor); and
● Inlet and outlet photographs.
Once the inspection is complete SEE will provide the collected data in .shp ﬁle format for integration into the 
City’s existing GIS database.   
As referenced in your recent email correspondence (11/13/26), we are providing a cost to complete this work for a 
total of 420 crossings, with a separate cost line item for each additional crossing. This additional per crossing cost 
will be billed (following approval) for any currently unmapped crossings that are located and inspected while 
completing the inspections of the 420 currently identi ﬁed crossings.  This price does not include any report 
writing or additional data analysis. If these services are requested, they will be detailed under a separate scope 
and budget.

To: Finance Committee 
From: Allen Ward, Deputy Director of Budget and Purchasing 
Subject: Casella Recycling, LLC Single Sort Recycling Contract Extension 
Date: November 23, 2026 
At the May 10, 2021, meeting, the Finance Committee approved an extension of the Casella Single Sort 
Recycling contract through June 30, 2026.  As summarized in the PW Director’s memo, PW has been in 
negotiations with Casella for Lewiston’s pricing of the next  Single Sort Recycling  contract extension 
through June 30, 2033, citing changes in the recyclables market and processing.    
As summarized in Casella’s attached Processing Fee Agreement, the maximum per-ton costs for Single 
Sort Recycling before market pricing rebate consideration through June 30, 2033 are as follows:  
July 1, 2027 – June 30th, 2028 - $60.00/ton 
July 1, 2028 – June 30th, 2033 - $105.00/ton 
For the reasons cited in his memo, the PW Director recommends approving the contract extension with 
pricing to phase in these costs for Lewiston. 
Funding for per-tonnage Single Sort Recycling costs starting in FY27 would be budgeted by PW in the 
Solid Waste operating budget. 
It is recommended to approve the Single Sort Recycling contract through June 30, 20 33, contained in 
Casella’s proposed agreement with maximum costs of $60/ton for FY28 and $105/ton through June 30, 
2033.

DATE: November 18, 2026 
To: Allen Ward, Deputy Director of Finance 
From: Kevin Gagne, Public Works Director 
Subject: Extension of Single Stream Recyclables Agreement 
Attached for consideration by the Finance Committee is a request to authorize the extension of 
Recycling Service Agreement for a 6-year period, January 1, 2027, to June 30, 2033. 
The original Casella Recycling Agreement, dated July 1, 2011, included two additional 5-year 
extensions.  In 2021, the Lewiston City Council approved to further extend the recycling 
agreement until 2026 with two (2) additional options to extend the recycling agreements (July 
2026 through June 2031 and July 2031 through June 2038), “subject to the mutual agreement 
of the parties as to the business terms of such extensions.” (see attached agreement dated July 
9, 2021). 
In spring of 2026, in preparation for the option to extend the recycling agreement that would be 
ending in June of 2026, Lewiston PW began discussion with Casella representatives.  The 
discussions took longer than we anticipated and we have had multiple 30-day extensions of the 
agreement to come to mutual agreement.  As expected, and predicted by former Director 
Brenchick in her 2021 memo, Casella originally proposed to start charging Lewiston for 
processing recycling.  Over the months of discussion, market pricing and specific Lewiston 
recycling commodity pricing was reviewed and Casella agreed to extend the no cost for 
processing until end of June 2027 and it was agreed to do a phase in of the processing fee the 
following budget year (FY2028) at $60 per ton and a 3rd year (FY 2029) processing fee of $105 
per ton.  Other communities have been paying processing fees at $105 or higher for years and 
while we have had no costs, it is reasonable to expect to pay for some processing as the 
commodities market for recycling is not as valuable as it once was. 
To restate previous recycling memos, when these original agreements were signed, the 
recyclables market was thriving, and revenues would be shared back and forth according to the 
agreement.  Today, the market has drastically plummeted for all recyclable materials, with the 
exception of metals. Many factors in the economy added to this decline; however, the changes 
in Chinese policies are at the top of the list.  In January of 2018, China banned the import of 
single sort recycling due to the surge of soiled and contaminated materials. This policy change 
led to a global shift in how materials tossed in the recycling bin are processed. Casella has dealt 
with these changes for us as part of their original agreement.  Since 2018, the market rates 
have not rebounded to what they once were, and Casella has been augmenting Lewiston 
recycling to maximize value of the different materials.   
9
I have discussed the proposed increase with City Administration throughout the discussion with 
Casella and they support my recommendation to approve the proposed recycling agreement for 
our next term, ending June 2033. 
 
Cc: Megan Bates, Deputy Director of Operations and Maintenance 
  John Kuchinski, Environmental Specialist/Solid Waste Superintendent

RECYCLING SERVICES  AGREEMENT 
 
This Recycling Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is made and entered into this 1st day of July, 
2026 (the "Effective Date"), by and between The City of Lewiston, Maine  ("Generator") and, Casella 
Recycling, LLC ("Processor"). 
 
In consideration of the covenants and undertakings of the parties hereto and other good and valuable 
consideration, the sufficiency and receipt of which is hereby acknowledged, Generator and Processor 
hereby agree as follows:  
 
1. DEFINITIONS 
 
“Facility" means the processing facility located at 424 River Road, Lewiston, ME 04240.  
 
Hours of Operation at the Facility shall be as follows:  
 
Monday through Friday  8am to 4pm 
 
Holiday Closings: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, 4th of July, Labor Day, 
   Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day.  
 
Should additional deliveries be required, arrangements can be made through mutual agreement between parties.  
 
"Single Stream Residential Mix" means recyclable fibers and containers collected in a single collection container 
or vehicle. Please see Schedule B for complete list of Acceptable Recyclable Materials and Unacceptable 
Material. 
 
 
2. RESPONSIBILITIES OF  GENERATOR 
 
Generator shall deliver or cause to be delivered to the Facility all Single Stream Residential Mix listed in 
Section 1, above, received by collections from the surrounding municipalities and commercial 
establishments. 
 
Acceptable/Unacceptable  Materials 
 
Generator shall comply with the descriptions of  Acceptable Recyclable Materials attached hereto as 
Schedule B, and shall deliver only Acceptable Materials to the Facility.  Any material that is not "Acceptable 
Recyclable Materials" is "Unacceptable  Material".  Processor shall have the right to inspect all inbound loads 
from the Generator. Upon inspection, Processor may downgrade loads which contain or appear to contain 
contaminants. The entire cost arising from Generator's delivery of any Unacceptable Load (including without 
limitation, transportation, re-loading, clean-up, alternate disposal and the like) shall be the sole responsibility of 
the Generator. Title to Unacceptable Material shall not pass from Generator to Processor.   Generator shall 
indemnify, hold Processor harmless, and promptly reimburse Processor for all damages, losses and expenses, 
including reasonable attorney’s fees and federal, state or local fines and penalties, resulting from the inclusion of 
any hazardous waste or hazardous materials in any load delivered by the Generator to the Facility, regardless of 
any allegation that Processor should have discovered the inclusion of such materials prior to accepting delivery of 
such load.   
 
 
 
 
 
12
3. RESPONSIBILITIES OF PROCESSOR 
 
Processor will receive, process, and market all Single Stream Residential Mix delivered to the Facility by the 
Generator. Processor will provide Generator with a monthly report which shall indicate the date, time, and net 
weight for each load, a report of the total tons received for that calendar month, and a billing summary.   
 
4. TERM 
 
Initial Term. The initial term of this Agreement shall commence on January 1, 2027 and shall expire on June 30, 
2033 (the "Initial Term "). 
 
   Extensions. This Agreement may be extended for an additional term of five (5) years upon mutually acceptable 
terms and conditions and agreement of the parties.   
5. PRICE 
 
There will be no charge ($0.00) to Generator for the processing and marketing of Single Stream Residential Mix 
from January 1, 2027 to June 30th , 2027.  Beginning July 1, 2027, pricing shall be as described in Schedule A.  
All invoices shall be paid net thirty (30) days from date of invoice .

SCHEDULE A 
PRICING TERMS 
Single Stream Pricing Formula:  
ACR - Threshold = Rebate (Charge)  
 
Average Commodity Revenue (ACR) - means the current market value for each recyclable commodity (including residue tons) 
multiplied by the product mix percentage for each recyclable commodity tons from that facility for the residential line of bu siness 
over the same month, less any direct costs of Processor related to transportation, storage, or marketing of product.   In addition, if 
there is a material change in the ACR during any thirty-day period, the Processor reserves the right to make an immediate 
adjustment to the ACR. 
ACR pricing provisions include: 
 
• Pricing for fiber will be determined by the New England market price published in the first 
monthly issue of the “Price Watch: Recovered Paper – Domestic” section of the PPI Pulp 
& Paper Week (“PPI”) and will include Sorted Residential Paper and News (SRN #56), 
OCC (#11) and Mix Paper (#54). 
 
• Pricing for containers, less glass and residue, will  be determined by the National market 
price published in the first issue of Recycling Markets.Net ( www.recyclingmarkets.net) 
and will include Natural HDPE baled, Color HDPE baled, PET Baled, PP postconsumer  
baled, Mix Bulky Rigids baled, Aluminum (sorted  and baled) and Steel cans (sorted and 
baled). 
 
• The value of MRF finished  Residue will be determined by the market rate cost of disposal. 
The value of processed Glass will be determined by the market rate of recycling processed 
glass. 
 
Rebate (Charge) - means the percentage of value paid to the Generator when the ACR is greater than the Threshold. When the 
Rebate is negative, each dollar below the Threshold will be charged to the Generator. 
 
Rebate Split = 50% to Generator when ACR is above Threshold 
 
Threshold July 1, 2027 – June 30 th, 2028 = $60.00 means the base rate required to process Recyclable Materials (including 
increases in labor expenses, costs to cover capital investments and other costs that may impact the processing).  
 
Threshold July 1, 2028 – June 30 th, 2033 = $105.00 means the base rate required to process Recyclable Materials (including 
increases in labor expenses, costs to cover capital investments and other costs that may impact the processing). Threshold shall be 
subject to an annual cost of living adjustment on January 1st each year equal to 3%. 
 
 
Threshold for material received above 20% contamination will be charged to Generator at market rate.
